claims.claim: Croatia has no wealth tax

sources.name: PwC: Croatia, individual, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 27 August 2026. "There are no net wealth/worth taxes in Croatia." "Inheritance and gift tax is payable on cash, monetary claims, and securities, as well as movable property if individual market value of movable property exceeds EUR 6,700"; "Tax is determined by the Tax Administration at the rate of 4%"; "A taxpayer is a legal entity or an individual who inherits or receives a gift in Croatia." "Certain exemptions exist."

sources.name: PwC: quick chart, net wealth/worth tax rates
sources.says: Headline net wealth/worth tax rate: Greece "NA" (last reviewed 08 September 2026), Cyprus "NA" (04 August 2026), Croatia "NA" (27 August 2026), Bulgaria "NA" (02 August 2026). "NA" is defined as "Not Applicable (i.e. the territory does not have the indicated tax or requirement)".

claims.claim: Dividends, interest and gains pay a 12% final rate

sources.name: PwC: Croatia, individual, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 27 August 2026. Under "Income from capital (final income)": "Income from interest, dividends, capital gains: 12%." Taxable gains are "Capital gains income realised from disposal of acquired financial assets and alienated within two years". Interest from bonds, "irrespective of the type of bond or bond issuer", is not counted as interest income.

claims.note: PwC adds that bond interest is not taxed as interest income; the profile does not say so and was left. Porezna uprava's page on capital income was not searched for; PwC's page is dated August 2026. scores.tax stays 4 (no wealth tax and ≤15% on dividends).

claims.claim: Croatia's inheritance tax is 4%, and the spouse and descendants are exempt

sources.name: Zakon.hr: Zakon o lokalnim porezima (Local Taxes Act), consolidated text
sources.says: Consolidated with NN 115/16, 101/17, 114/22, 114/23 and 152/24. Art. 4: "Porez na nasljedstva i darove plaća se na gotov novac, novčane tražbine i vrijednosne papire (vrijednosnice)" and on movables above 6,700 euros. Art. 5: the taxpayer is a person who "na području Republike Hrvatske naslijede, prime na dar ili steknu po drugoj osnovi bez naknade imovinu" (inherits in the territory of Croatia). Art. 8: "Porez na nasljedstva i darove plaća se po stopi od 4%." Art. 9: not paid by "bračni drug, potomci i preci koji čine uspravnu liniju te posvojenici i posvojitelji" (spouse, descendants and ascendants in the direct line, adoptees and adopters). First 100,000 characters of the page read.

sources.name: Porezna uprava: inheritance and gifts tax, general rules, rates and taxpayer
sources.says: Date of update 8 January 2025. "inheritance and gifts tax is paid at the rate of 4%"; the taxpayer is a person who inherits or receives property without compensation in Croatia; cash, claims and securities are taxed, movables only "if individual market value of movables is greater than 6.700,00 eura". The page lists no family exemption and says nothing about property abroad.

sources.name: PwC: Croatia, individual, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 27 August 2026. "There are no net wealth/worth taxes in Croatia." "Inheritance and gift tax is payable on cash, monetary claims, and securities, as well as movable property if individual market value of movable property exceeds EUR 6,700"; "Tax is determined by the Tax Administration at the rate of 4%"; "A taxpayer is a legal entity or an individual who inherits or receives a gift in Croatia." "Certain exemptions exist."

claims.note: The Tax Administration's English page gives the rate but not the family exemption; the statute (art. 9) was read on zakon.hr, a private consolidation, not on Narodne novine. It also exempts ascendants. localTaxes.ts agrees.

sources.says: October 2022, summarising a Tax Authority opinion: "The Tax Authority emphasizes that the payment of inheritance and gifts taxes is based on the territorial principle."; "the provisions of the Law on Local Taxes do not apply to the inheritance located abroad."; heirs of funds in foreign banks "are not liable to pay inheritance and gifts taxes in the Republic of Croatia."

claims.claim: There is no retiree or property route: the Interior Ministry's grounds for temporary stay are family, study, work, digital nomads and "other purposes"

sources.name: Croatian Ministry of the Interior: temporary stay of third-country nationals
sources.says: Undated (copyright 2026). Purposes listed: family reunification, secondary school or university, scientific research, humanitarian grounds, life partnership, work, posted workers, long-term residents of another EEA state, other purposes, digital nomads. For other purposes: "Temporary stay is granted for a period of up to one year"; a new application "only after six months have passed from the expiry of temporary stay that was granted for other purposes". Applicants must "have funds to support themselves" and "have health insurance". No retiree, pensioner or property-owner ground.

claims.note: The ministry lists ten purposes; the profile names five and leaves out research, humanitarian grounds, life partnership, posted workers and long-term residents of another EEA state, none of which is a retiree route. Summary, drawback 1 and scores.visa 1 agree; Split's `why` agrees.

sources.name: Zakon.hr: Act on compulsory health insurance and health care of foreigners in Croatia
sources.says: Text in force from 16.04.2022 (NN 46/22). Art. 6(1): a third-country national granted temporary stay "obvezan je podnijeti prijavu na obvezno zdravstveno osiguranje područnoj službi Zavoda" within eight days and "je obveznik plaćanja doprinosa za obvezno zdravstveno osiguranje u skladu s posebnim zakonom" (pays the contribution under a separate law). Digital nomads are exempt from registering. Art. 7 sets a one-time payment on the lowest base for up to 12 months as a condition of insured status. No rate or amount is in the Act.

claims.note: hzzo.hr was not found by search for this question; the Act was read on zakon.hr, which shows the 2022 text. Not in the profile and not added: the Act makes registration compulsory within eight days and sets a one-time payment of up to 12 months of contributions as a condition of insured status.
